verses.text: צַ֚ו אֶת־בְּנֵ֣י יִשְׂרָאֵ֔ל וְאָמַרְתָּ֖ אֲלֵהֶ֑ם אֶת־קָרְבָּנִ֞י לַחְמִ֜י לְאִשַּׁ֗י רֵ֚יחַ נִֽיחֹחִ֔י תִּשְׁמְר֖וּ לְהַקְרִ֥יב לִ֖י בְּמוֹעֲדֽוֹ׃
וְאָמַרְתָּ֣ לָהֶ֔ם זֶ֚ה הָאִשֶּׁ֔ה אֲשֶׁ֥ר תַּקְרִ֖יבוּ לַיהֹוָ֑ה כְּבָשִׂ֨ים בְּנֵֽי־שָׁנָ֧ה תְמִימִ֛ם שְׁנַ֥יִם לַיּ֖וֹם עֹלָ֥ה תָמִֽיד׃

verses.key: Numbers 28:4 (fragment, page a / s54, last line)

verses.text: תַּעֲשֶׂ֣ה בַבֹּקֶר וְאֵת֙ הַכֶּ֣בֶשׂ הַשֵּׁנִ֔י תַּעֲשֶׂ֖ה בֵּ֥ין הָעַרְבָּֽיִם׃
וַעֲשִׂירִ֧ית הָאֵיפָ֛ה סֹ֖לֶת לְמִנְחָ֑ה בְּלוּלָ֥ה בְּשֶׁ֛מֶן כָּתִ֖ית רְבִיעִ֥ת הַהִֽין׃
עֹלַ֖ת תָּמִ֑יד הָעֲשֻׂיָה֙ בְּהַ֣ר סִינַ֔י לְרֵ֣יחַ נִיחֹ֔חַ אִשֶּׁ֖ה לַיהֹוָֽה׃
וְנִסְכּוֹ֙ רְבִיעִ֣ת הַהִ֔ין לַכֶּ֖בֶשׂ הָאֶחָ֑ד בַּקֹּ֗דֶשׁ הַסֵּ֛ךְ נֶ֥סֶךְ שֵׁכָ֖ר לַיהֹוָֽה׃
וְאֵת֙ הַכֶּ֣בֶשׂ הַשֵּׁנִ֔י תַּעֲשֶׂ֖ה בֵּ֣ין הָעַרְבָּ֑יִם כְּמִנְחַ֨ת הַבֹּ֤קֶר וּכְנִסְכּוֹ֙ תַּעֲשֶׂ֔ה אִשֵּׁ֛ה רֵ֥יחַ נִיחֹ֖חַ לַיהֹוָֽה׃
וְשָׁחַ֨ט אֹת֜וֹ עַ֣ל יֶ֧רֶךְ הַמִּזְבֵּ֛חַ צָפֹ֖נָה לִפְנֵ֣י יְהֹוָ֑ה וְזָרְק֡וּ בְּנֵ֩י אַהֲרֹן הַכֹּהֲנִים אֶת־דָּמ֥וֹ עַל־הַמִּזְבֵּ֖חַ סָבִֽיב׃

uncertainties: Num 28:4 בַבֹּקֶר (page b, line 1): I saw no zaqef dots above this word. I saw a caret/angle-shaped mark below it, possibly an etnachta shape or a mahpakh-like angle. It is unresolved, so I left the accent out of the text. It needs an enlarged crop.
Num 28:4 אֶחָד֙ (page a, last line): I took the mark as pashta, but I can't confidently tell whether it sits above the word (pashta) or below it. Unresolved.

Num 28:2 נִֽיחֹחִ֔י: the zaqef qatan is not clearly visible over this word in the crop. One vertical two-dot mark sits in the gap between lines 2–4 near תִּשְׁמְרוּ / לָהֶם, and I could not tell which word it belongs to. The meteg under nun is also uncertain.
Num 28:2 לְאִשַּׁ֗י: I am fairly sure of the revia dot above shin. The vowel under shin (patah) is hard to see.
Num 28:2 תִּשְׁמְר֖וּ and לְהַקְרִ֥יב / לִ֖י: I read tipcha / mercha / tipcha from small slanted strokes. I couldn't confirm which way they slant at this resolution.
Num 28:3 הָאִשֶּׁ֔ה and לַיהֹוָ֑ה: there may be a meteg under he / lamed, but I didn't see it clearly, so it is left out of the text.
Num 28:3 בְּנֵֽי־: a meteg under nun is probable but faint. I read the darga under שָׁנָ֧ה (zigzag) and the tevir under תְמִימִ֛ם from small marks. I saw no dagesh in תְ of תְמִימִם.
Num 28:5 סֹ֖לֶת: I'm unsure whether there is a tipcha under samekh.
Num 28:6 הָעֲשֻׂיָה֙: I'm unsure whether there is a meteg under the first he. The zaqef over נִיחֹ֔חַ is not clearly seen; it could also be absent or a different accent.
Num 28:7 בַּקֹּ֗דֶשׁ: I'm fairly sure of the revia dot. I could not verify the dagesh in initial bet.
Num 28:8 תַּעֲשֶׂ֔ה (second occurrence): I'm fairly sure of the zaqef. For אִשֵּׁ֛ה, the mark under shin (tevir) is unclear.

Lev 1:11 בְּנֵ֩י / אַהֲרֹן: a small ring-shaped mark sits above, between בני and the ornamental אהרן. I transcribed it as telisha qetana on בני. It could also be telisha gedola belonging to אַהֲרֹן. I couldn't make out the accent on אַהֲרֹן itself, so it is left out.
Lev 1:11 וְזָרְק֡וּ: I read pazer from a hooked mark above qof. A meteg under zayin may be present but is not confirmed.

Lev 1:11 הַכֹּהֲנִים: there is an accent mark under or near nun, but I couldn't identify it (possibly tevir), so it is left out. The accent under ayin of עַל־ (second occurrence) is also unclear, possibly a tipcha-like stroke, and is left out.
Throughout, I could not reliably confirm small dagesh dots (for example בֵּ in וַיְדַבֵּ֥ר, the dagesh in כֶּ, and בְּ in בְּמוֹעֲדוֹ) at this resolution.
observations: Every Divine Name is printed יְהֹוָה with holam on he, matching the earlier enlarged pass.
Num 28:2 starts mid-line on page a (צַ֚ו after לֵּאמֹֽר׃). The ornamental large alef in אֶת־קָרְבָּנִ֞י is a typographic flourish, not a different letter.
Physical verse 28:4 is split: אֶת־הַכֶּ֤בֶשׂ אֶחָד֙ ends page a (s54), and תַּעֲשֶׂ֣ה בַבֹּקֶר … הָעַרְבָּֽיִם׃ opens page b (s55).
Lev 1:11 is headed by the marginal source note 'ויקרא א׳ י״א.' and uses an ornamental alef in אַהֲרֹן.
Each verse ends with the sof pasuq ׃ printed as a diamond-shaped colon.
Unresolved items need a tight, enlarged crop to settle: especially בַבֹּקֶר (28:4), אֶחָד (28:4), נִיחֹחִי (28:2), and the telisha / אַהֲרֹן accent in Lev 1:11.
